transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-21 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE); Maya Chen (Redwood SE); Lucas Park (Redwood CSM); Derek Morales (Oceanic Head of MLOps); Priya Iyer (Oceanic VP Product); Sam Knight (Oceanic SRE); Ally Ruiz (Oceanic Finance)
Shared: Q2 health deck (link), pilot cost workbook (link), SOC2 + encryption whitepaper (link)

Summary notes (auto):
- Usage up 38% month-over-month due to product experiment; cost burn concentrated on long-context chat endpoint.
- Several latency spikes during peak hours; likely due to batching and eviction behavior on their on-prem cluster.
- Customer leaning toward Dedicated capacity but wants clearer committed pricing and security certs.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. uh, we'll run through the Q2 health snapshot and then drill into a couple of the items Priya flagged last week, mainly cost and latency. mm-hm?
[00:18] Derek: yep thanks Jordan. quick note, running late on the deck for us but we have the workbook, so cool.
[00:22] Maya: great, i'll share my screen with the benchmark heatmap in a sec. but first quick context, usage growth is mostly the recommendation assistant and the long‑run chat flows, so token per call is up.
[00:37] Priya: correct, the assistant tests pushed up context length, and Finance wants to see projection, cause it's ~3x token burn on peak days.
[00:45] Ally: yeah, from our side the question is committed or bursts — we need predictability for budgeting.
[00:52] Jordan: totally, that's the exact tradeoff we've seen — hosted API gives you flexibility but less predictability on unit cost under burst; Dedicated gives headroom and flatter unit economics. we sketched three commit bands in the pricing workbook. i'll send the more granular sheet after this.
[01:08] Sam: one technical thing — we've seen 95th percentile latency jump around 4pm PST last thursday; maybe related to KV cache churn? sometimes the logs say "K V cash" which is odd in the exporter, sorry transcription note.
[01:24] Maya: yeah i saw that, and i suspect cache eviction + small batch mixing; on our Redwood Dedicate (sic) runtime we can tune prefetch and cache retention per model. but i want to run their actual on‑prem workload to be sure.
[01:40] Derek: can Redwood run a 24 hour pass that mirrors our spike pattern? we can provide traces and the script.
[01:46] Maya: absolutely, if Sam can give us the traffic profile we'll schedule an isolated benchmark. recommend we run with and without quantization to see perf/cost delta.
[01:56] Sam: i'll dump the traces and put them in the shared drive today.
[02:00] Priya: security — our security team asked specifically about KMS integration, SSO/SAML, and audit logs. we also need SOC 2 evidence to speed legal.
[02:09] Jordan: yep we have a SOC 2 package; also we support customer KMS and HSM flows for private deployments. i'll include the whitepaper link. for hosted customers we encrypt at rest and in transit and we have RBAC and audit hooks.
[02:24] Priya: for private, VPC peering and no internet egress is important — can Redwood support airgap or on‑prem package?
[02:33] Maya: we do have a private deployment option — customers can run the private control plane in their VPC or on‑prem with our bundle. small caveat: some tooling (managed analytics) needs optional connectivity; we can walk through a hardened plan.
[02:45] Derek: timeline question — if we choose Dedicated with a commit, how long to provision and what are SLOs?
[02:52] Jordan: typical lead is 2–4 weeks for Dedicated pool with our reservation process; SLA will be part of the commercial contract — we're targeting 99.9% for critical endpoints and we map latency SLOs per model.
[03:06] Ally: and pricing — is there a discount curve if we commit 6 vs 12 months?
[03:10] Jordan: yes, the workbook shows approximate delta; bigger bands give steeper discounts and burst credits. i'll attach a version that includes 6/12/24 month bands.
[03:20] Lucas: also, on usage reporting — Derek we still need API token access to pull their token-level logs; i pinged but didn't see the token.
[03:28] Derek: sorry yeah i'll get that to you by EOD.
[03:32] Priya: quick product question — can we pin a specific model version for a rollout? we want consistent quality and an easy rollback.
[03:40] Maya: yes, the platform supports model pinning and canary rollouts; we also have a fallback mechanism to a cheaper variant if capacity gets constrained. some of the names in the docs are a little off in the transcript, but that's the gist.
[03:54] Priya: are there any quality regressions we've seen when quantizing? we tested int8 and saw some hallucination increases in the summarization flow.
[04:04] Maya: good call — quantization can slightly shift probabilities; we have guidance on eval sets and regression detection in Redwood Optimize. i'd recommend running a small eval suite pre‑ and post‑quantization.
[04:18] Sam: on the latency spikes, i want to call out network egress on our side — last Friday we had a flurry of small requests from many clients that created a lot of tiny batches. could batching policies help?
[04:29] Maya: yes, adaptive batching is one lever. we can suggest batch windows and dynamic thresholds; also prefix caching helps for repeated conversation starts.
[04:36] Derek: is there a risk if we use prefix cache for PII sensitive content? we need to ensure cache is ephemeral and encrypted.
[04:45] Jordan: cache is encrypted at rest and optional TTL controls exist; for regulated flows you can opt out of caching or use customer-managed encryption keys.
[04:56] Priya: legal asked about data residency; we need audit logs retained for 365+ days for a particular line of business. can Redwood increase retention?
[05:05] Lucas: we can extend retention as an add-on and ship logs to their archive bucket via secure transfer. will put details in follow up.
[05:14] Ally: finance asks: if we go Dedicated, how do token credits work if we don't use the full band?
[05:20] Jordan: unused capacity can be consumed as burst credits or rolled to future months depending on contract; we'll model scenarios in the workbook.
[05:28] Priya: going back to the bench runs — what metrics will Redwood capture in the 24 hour run? latency percentiles, P50 P90 P95 P99, token cost, throughput, and error rate?
[05:37] Maya: yes and also memory usage, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, and a token‑level cost report. we'll publish a CSV with per-minute buckets.
[05:46] Sam: can you also capture cold start times when we start new workers? that's when our tail latency spikes.
[05:51] Maya: good call. we'll instrument cold start and warmup profiles.
[05:55] Derek: operational question — if we hit an incident, what's Redwood's escalation path? we need an oncall contact and RTO expectations.
[06:03] Jordan: our enterprise contracts include an incident escalation flow with a named SE and a phone/pager rota; typical RTO depends on the severity but we target fast triage and mitigation.
[06:14] Priya: tradeoff conversation — we need to balance cost and latency for our customers; if we accept slightly higher tail latency, can we reduce cost materially?
[06:23] Maya: yes batching and longer batch windows reduce per‑token cost but increase tail latency; quantization lowers GPU memory and cost with a modest quality hit. the Optimize toolkit gives scenario projections.
[06:36] Ally: finance wants clear examples — can we see a 3 scenarios table: minimal commit, medium commit, and full commit with expected monthly bill?
[06:45] Jordan: yes i'll build that as part of the pricing deliverable.
[06:49] Lucas: i'll add a note to include projected ROI in terms of cheaper tokens vs feature velocity risk.
[06:55] Derek: on customer side gating to prod: we need a stability window of two weeks with no P1s and a P95 below 400ms for our core flow. is that realistic?
[07:04] Maya: P95 400ms depends on model size and sequence length; for medium‑context models it's achievable with Dedicated and tuned batching. we'll run the bench to validate.
[07:16] Priya: any concerns about bringing in a third party for SOC or security attestation? we've had auditors ask for vendor attestations.
[07:24] Jordan: we can provide SOC reports and help coordinate vendor questionnaires; we also have security architecture reviews with our security team.
[07:33] Ally: last thing from finance — can we get cost runbooks for anomalous days? e.g., steps to quickly throttle or reroute to cheaper models.
[07:42] Maya: yes that's part of the cost playbook; runbooks include automatic fallback policies and throttles per route.
[07:49] Derek: ok sounds good. let's recap next steps.

Recap and explicit next steps (auto-capture):
- Jordan: send updated pilot pricing + commit bands and 6/12/24 month scenarios (due 2026-06-25)
- Maya: schedule + run 24h benchmark using Oceanic traces, include quantization and cold start analysis (target 2026-06-28)
- Lucas: follow up on usage reporting access and send how-to for API token (due 2026-06-23)
- Jordan: attach SOC2/KMS/HSM whitepaper and VPC deployment doc in follow up email (ASAP)

[08:12] Priya: thanks everyone, we'll review and come back with a preferred commit band next week.
[08:18] Jordan: thanks all, we'll get the artifacts over.

(transcript notes: occasional speaker labels may be off; words like "Dedicate" instead of "Dedicated" and "K V cash" instead of "KV cache" are transcription artifacts.)
